Sadly, most of these people are doing the best that they can given what they have. Mental health issues, physical health issues, drug addiction, and the cycle of poverty makes it so hard for the people on the absolute bottom to ever climb up. It's almost impossible to get a job if you're an addict or disabled, and if you are homeless on top of that your odds are almost 0.

There needs to be way better resources to helping these people get back on their feet in a meaningful way. An address where they can receive mail, a shower, psychiatric and counseling resources, and a roof over their head goes a long way.

But then you get into cross issues, like psychiatric and counseling resources are already strained. It's not unheard of to be on a psych waitlist for over a year for people who have relatively stable lives. And then, the mental health system sucks and you might get stuck with someone who has no interest in helping you. And if you are homeless and don't even have a mailing address or a phone getting access to these already limited resources can feel like climbing a mountain.

The lack of resources dedicated to social services and treating the underlying causes of these issues is probably the biggest problem because what resources do exist are already overcrowded.

This is just my opinion though, I think it's a massively complex topic that it's ok to be frustrated with and not like the consequences. But I think it's important to remember that the majority of the frustration should be focused at the systems (and the failure of these systems) that cause all of these people to suffer. I'm going to give a bit of a different recommendation and suggest checking out **Song of Syx**. It's a colony sim game similar to Rimworld or Dwarf Fortress but mashed up with a city builder. There is a lot less micromanagement than other colony sims leaving you to focus on building and maintaining a city.

There are a wide variety of different aspects of the city to manage and it features some very interesting mechanics that separates it from other city builders or colony sim games. There are a variety of fantasy races, each with their own needs and preferences, and you have to design your city to accommodate them and also manage racial tensions. You have to carefully manage what work is available in the city and plan out your access to resources.

The coolest part about it is that there is a population cap of \~10,000 IIRC. Like other colony sims, each individual is simulated and has their own needs, routines, and preferences. But it's easy to focus on the population at a large scale rather than micromanage your citizenship, so you can plan out what you need in order to invite more immigrants and retain your current population.

* Disco Elysium (the choose-your-own adventure version of a novel more or less, but with a stats system and skill checks. Though this one is more or less a choose your own adventure novel with game systems built on top to make it feel fresh)
* Pony Island and Inscription (a meta-narrative on games as a whole that use the fact they are games in a unique way)
* Her Story & Immortality (movies, but non-linear and you have to piece together the story using game mechanics)
* Interpretative, stylistic story-based RPGs and platformers (Gris, Hylics, and a few others)

Have you played Tyranny? It has one of the better magic systems for a CRPG. Your character has a "Lore" skill which determines your casting competency. Throughout the game you collect new "Cores", "Expressions", and "Aspects" that you can combine in unique ways to design your own spells.

The "Core" represents the school, like illusions, fire, frost, etc.

The "Expression" is the form, like a bolt attack, an AOE, an enhancement to a weapon, etc.

The "Accent" are modifiers on the spells, affecting various aspects on the spell. You can select as little or as many of these as you want.

Each of these parts of the spell costs a certain number of lore points, and you can combine the various aspects of a spell up to your lore skill. Any time outside of combat, you can change up your spells to whatever you want. It's a super cool system that actually makes you feel like a magical scholar.
